title: Paper Towels 6-roll

drivers.name: Store closure (Mon)
drivers.evidence: Store closed Monday; no prior closure data, but similar closures in retail reduce weekly sales ~20% on average. No other evidence of impact from price or events.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 96.6. No events are scheduled, but the store is closed Monday, reducing the selling window. Price is 4.5% above regular, which typically suppresses demand. Historical data shows no Halloween lift (noise-adjusted x1.0). A price increase to 10.32 previously (2026-09-28, 2026-10-05) had no impact (x1.00 vs baseline). The only driver is the store closure, which likely reduces sales by ~20% (1 day lost in 7-day week). No promotion or seasonal lift. The classical model’s x1.00 is correct, but the closure requires a downward adjustment. Shrink toward 1.0 due to low evidence for closure impact.

brief:
PRODUCT: Paper Towels 6-roll | category Household | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-10-19 to 2026-10-25 (2 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 10.32 (+4.5% vs regular price 9.88)
  planner notes: Store closed Monday for renovation

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 96.6 | 5%-95%: 62.8 - 233.4 | 10%-90%: 67.4 - 191.3

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-23% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
